title: How Much the Motors Can Give: Torque Limits and Heat in an Arm, the Payload That Fits at a Pose, and the Fastest a Move Can Be Made and Repeated

artifact.note: what the motors of an arm can give: a motor at each joint with a torque constant at the output, a resistance, a thermal resistance and capacity, a peak and a continuous torque; the current and the heat of a torque and the time to the temperature limit in closed form; the largest payload at a pose that every joint can hold (a linear problem in the one mass, with an interval for each joint); the torques of a quintic move and their largest and root mean square values; the shortest duration of the move that keeps the largest torque within the peak and the root mean square torque within the continuous limit; and the temperature a move repeated with a wait reaches
